input.diff:
diff --git a/distribution/install.sh b/distribution/install.sh
index 331db68..752a1f3 100755
--- a/distribution/install.sh
+++ b/distribution/install.sh
@@ -135,7 +135,12 @@ trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"; [ -z "$tmp_out" ] || rm -f "$tmp_out"' EXIT
 # dies with its own sentence around that cause.
 fetch_url() { # $1 = URL, $2 = destination
 	fetch_error=""
+	# Send GITHUB_TOKEN when set, so users behind shared IPs get the
+	# authenticated rate limit instead of the anonymous one.
+	auth=""
+	[ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ] && auth="Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
 	status=$(curl --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' -sSL \
+		${auth:+-H "$auth"} \
+		-o "$2" -w '%{http_code}' "$1") || {
 		-o "$2" -w '%{http_code}' "$1") || {
 		fetch_error="failed to fetch $1; check the connection and retry"
 		return 1

content.text:
The patch reads GITHUB_TOKEN and sends it as an Authorization header. ADR-0585 forbids this: "install.sh ... does not read GITHUB_TOKEN". I didn't run any of the checks, so their results are unknown.

{"verdict": "violates", "decisions": ["ADR-0585"], "checks": ["token set: no Authorization header anywhere (GITHUB_TOKEN never rides a request)"], "check_outcomes": {"token set: no Authorization header anywhere (GITHUB_TOKEN never rides a request)": "unknown", "drift guard: install.sh consults no GitHub API endpoint (ADR-0585)": "unknown", "no case made a GitHub API request (ADR-0585)": "unknown"}}
